Topic 2.2: Reading readiness.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading readiness., part of READING 2.1 Book handling. (2 lessons) By the end of the sub strand the learner  in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: What are the different things found near our school? 2. Which letter sounds sound almost similar?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognize pictures of things found in the neighbourhood,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading readiness. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

B. interpret familiar pictures correctly,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading readiness. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. chant rhymes on letter sounds and letter names,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading readiness. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. enjoy participating in pre- reading activities. • Identify pictures of things found in the neighbourhood from the writing board, charts, books, flash cards or digital devices. Learners with manipulation difficulties could identify the pictures of things found in the environment by pointing or verbally. ● Talk about the pictures collaboratively. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech to express their views. ● Read letters of the alphabet in purposive groups and as individuals from charts. 1. Which letter sounds sound almost similar? 17 ● Read letter sounds in purposive pairs and as individuals from charts. ● Chant rhymes on letter sounds and letter names. Learners with speech difficulties could listen to the others' chanting while identifying the letter sound and letter names from a chart or flash cards.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading readiness. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
